reason: The passage (Exodus 2:16-22) depicts Moses meeting the daughters of Jethro, a Midianite priest, at a well. The speakers are Midianites (Jethro and his daughters), not Hebrew people voicing collective criticism. The dialogue is descriptive and grateful in tone—the daughters relate how an Egyptian (Moses) rescued them from shepherds and watered their flock, and Jethro simply asks why they returned early. There is no criticism voiced against Hebrew leaders or against Yahweh in this passage. The text is a narrative account of Moses' encounter with Jethro's family, not a passage featuring the Hebrew people expressing dissatisfaction.
